name: r5-m07
statement: By RL step 100 the Olmo-3.1 RL-Zero-Math policy differs from the base almost only in its opening: on the plain prompt it now starts most answers with the RL cue ' line!\n\nOkay', and once it has done that it behaves like the cued base (same loop rate, same loop problems, same finished-answer accuracy, the base's own 'Answer:' format), so its T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 cap hits climb toward the cued base's 119 because a cue-style opening loops more than a plain one, not because the policy has become sharper.
scope: Covers allenai/Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math at step_0100 (and, more weakly, step_0400) against allenai/Olmo-3-1025-7B, on MATH-500 with the plain prompt at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 / cap 16,384 (the RLN-3 r3 cells), plus the base's own plain answers in the same setting. It does not cover the final checkpoint (step 2,800), whose weights and activations have moved well past the base and which loops rarely; T 1.0, where rule-A loops vanish for every model; the harder set; or the theta(a) weight blends, except as indirect support. It says nothing about the 11-point gap at AI2's setting.

imports.finding: An RL-trained steering vector mostly acts as a bias on the first generated token; prefixing that token ('To') gives about 75 % of the vector's gain.
imports.how: Gives the precedent that the first thing RL installs can be an opening-token bias that a tiny weight change can carry. Here that bias is the cue ' line!\n\nOkay', and it decides which register the rest of the answer is written in.

imports.finding: A behaviour the base already has (code-style reasoning) goes from 65 % to about 90 % of responses within 15 RL steps, and that switch carries most of the gain.
imports.how: Shows that an existing surface behaviour can take over within the first few RL steps. The mechanism puts the cue opening in that role by step 100, while internal activations are still at the base's noise floor.

explains.how: This is the loop rate a cue-style opening produces in the base at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, and step 100 inherits it in proportion to how often it opens with the cue.
The plain base opens the cue far less often, so it loops less. Step 100's cap hits sit between the two base cells because it is a mixture of the two openings.
Step 100's internal computation is nearly the base's, so its behaviour change has to come from something small and early, such as the opening tokens, not from a reshaped policy.
Step 100's top-activating contexts sit at the noise floor relative to the base, which fits a change confined to a few opening logits.

explains.quote: 494 of 500 RL T 0.6 answers begin ' line'
explains.how: The cue is the opening RL eventually adopts almost always, so it is the natural first thing for RL to install.
The RL-minus-base divergence is concentrated at the opening positions (0.06-0.09 nats per token elsewhere), which is where this mechanism puts the early change.

A quarter of the RL weight difference already lifts plain answers to about the cued base's 410 at T 1.0, which is what you would expect if the first part of the RL change mainly installs the cue opening.

conflicts.quote: 'Answer:' line in 0-4 % of answers vs 39-46 % for base-like arms
conflicts.how: Partial RL-delta arms that recover accuracy also take on RL's boxed format. If step 100 behaved like such an arm it would drop the base's 'Answer:' line, but this mechanism says it keeps that line.

conflicts.quote: a=0.25 is +6.2 pts over base cue [3.0, 9.6]
conflicts.how: A small fraction of the RL difference adds accuracy even when the cue is already forced, so early RL is not only an opening change. Step 100 may carry some of that extra gain, which this mechanism leaves out.

rival: The strongest rival is r4-m10: early RL steps sharpen the token distribution, so loop tokens cross top-p 0.95's lock threshold more often. On that account cap hits rise across all of step 100's answers whatever their opening, finished accuracy rises, and loops appear at new problems. This mechanism instead confines the rise to the answers that open with the cue, matches their cap-hit rate to the cued base's, and keeps the base's format. The separating observation is the step-100 cap-hit rate split by opening (prediction 2): sharpening predicts about equal rates in the two groups, this mechanism predicts about the cued-base minus plain-base difference. A second separating observation is step 100 run with the cue forced (GPU prediction): this mechanism predicts the cued base's numbers, sharpening predicts more cap hits than 119. A length-growth rival (answers simply get longer) also predicts no difference by opening.

predictions.experiment: Share of step-100 plain MATH-500 answers at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 that open with the RL cue's first token 'line'. The sharpening rival (r4-m10) and the length rival leave the opening as the plain base's, near 0.
predictions.recipe: Fetch s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0100/P_math500.jsonl (aws s3 cp ... --profile iterate-ecr). Keep rows with sample == 0. If a problem_index appears more than once, keep the first row in file order. For each row, test whether text.lstrip() starts with the 4 characters 'line' (case-sensitive). Statistic: the number of rows that pass divided by the number of kept rows. Cap-hit rows count like any other row. Problems with no row are left out of the denominator.

predictions.experiment: Mechanism test: within the step-100 plain T 0.6 answers, the cap-hit rate of answers that open with 'line' minus the cap-hit rate of answers that do not. This mechanism expects about the cued-base minus plain-base gap (0.24 - 0.13 = 0.11). The nearest rival, policy sharpening that crosses top-p's lock threshold (r4-m10), raises cap hits whatever the opening and expects about 0.00. The length-growth rival also expects about 0.00.
predictions.recipe: Same file and filters as prediction 1 (s0100/P_math500.jsonl, sample == 0, first row per problem_index). Group A: rows where text.lstrip() starts with 'line'. Group B: all other kept rows. For each group, cap-hit rate = number of rows with cap_hit true divided by the group's row count. Statistic: rate(A) - rate(B). If either group has fewer than 20 rows, the prediction counts as refuted. Missing problems are left out.
predictions.refuted_by: measured below 0.02, or either group has fewer than 20 rows

predictions.experiment: Mechanism test on the plain base itself: in base-01's plain MATH-500 answers at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, the cap-hit rate of answers that open in the cue's register ('Okay' within the first 12 characters, e.g. '.\n\nOkay') minus the rate of the other answers. This mechanism says the register drives the loops and expects a clearly positive gap. A rival in which loops depend only on problem length or difficulty and not on the opening expects about 0.
predictions.recipe: Fetch s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (aws s3 cp ... --profile iterate-ecr). Keep rows with sample == 0 and the first row per problem_index. Group A: rows where the substring 'Okay' occurs in text[:12]. Group B: all other kept rows. For each group, cap-hit rate = number of rows with cap_hit true divided by the group's row count. Statistic: rate(A) - rate(B). If either group has fewer than 20 rows, the prediction counts as refuted. Missing problems are left out.
predictions.refuted_by: measured below 0.03, or either group has fewer than 20 rows

predictions.experiment: Share of step-100's finished plain T 0.6 answers that still state the result on an 'Answer:' line (the base's format). This mechanism expects a base-like share. A format-shift rival, in which early RL already moves the policy to RL's boxed format (RL share 0.00), expects near 0.
predictions.recipe: Same file and filters as prediction 1 (s0100/P_math500.jsonl, sample == 0, first row per problem_index). Keep only rows with cap_hit false. A row counts if any line of text, after str.lstrip(), starts with 'Answer:' (case-sensitive), where lines are text.split('\n'). Statistic: rows that count divided by finished rows. Missing problems and cap-hit rows are left out.

predictions.experiment: GPU: allenai/Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math at revision step_0100 (897c0ce4 is step_0400, 0a45720c is step_0100; use 0a45720c) with the opening cue ids [1584, 2268, 33413] after the 3.1 prompt, MATH-500 n = 500, one sample, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, cap 16,384, seed 1,000,000 + problem_index, vLLM via studies/rlneurons/jobs/run_cell.py on one H100, grader v3. Count cap hits. This mechanism says step 100 with the cue forced equals the cued base (119 cap hits, 354 right). Sharpening (r4-m10) expects more cap hits than the cued base.
predictions.refuted_by: cap hits below 98 or above 140, or grader-v3 right of 500 outside [330, 378]
